There are also several other local firms worth comparing, depending on whether your priority is negotiating a settlement, protecting business or investment assets, or making an agreement legally binding. ## Which firm has the strongest track record?

There is no reliable public dataset that compares actual settlement outcomes, the percentage of successful BFAs, or the amount of wealth protected across Ipswich firms. Based on verifiable specialist credentials and relevant experience, my ranking for your particular needs is\:

| Priority | Firm I'd approach first | Why |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Complex property division | Fallu McMillan | Two Accredited Family Law Specialists; specific business, trust and superannuation experience |
| High-value negotiations | Millwater Tyrrell | Explicit experience with complicated, high-value settlements and mediation |
| BFA-focused advice | Stanford Legal | Dedicated BFA and property settlement services |
| Interconnected business assets | McNamara Law | Family law plus commercial and estate services |


These are recommendations based on publicly documented expertise, not a verified ranking of case outcomes.

## An important distinction: BFA or consent orders?

Because you're already separating, ask each firm which mechanism best protects your position.

- **Binding financial agreement\:** A private agreement that can cover property division and spousal maintenance, subject to strict legal requirements.
- **Consent orders\:** Court orders formalising an agreed property settlement. These may be preferable for many post-separation settlements and are generally harder to challenge than a BFA.

Both parties generally need full financial disclosure, and each must obtain independent legal advice for a BFA to be binding. A poorly prepared agreement can be challenged later. [millwatertyrrell.com.au](https://millwatertyrrell.com.au/our-lawyers?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[millwatertyrrell.com.au](https://millwatertyrrell.com.au/orders-and-agreements?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[stanfordlegal.com.au](https://stanfordlegal.com.au/family-law/binding-financial-agreement?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## Questions to ask at your first consultation

I'd ask each shortlisted lawyer\:

1. How many complex property settlements have you personally handled involving businesses, trusts, multiple properties or substantial superannuation?
2. What is your experience drafting or challenging binding financial agreements, including agreements made after separation?
3. How would you identify and value the asset pool, account for liabilities, and assess contributions and future needs?
4. Would you recommend a BFA or consent orders in my circumstances, and why?
5. What are your estimated total legal fees for negotiation, mediation and, if necessary, court proceedings?

Ask for an itemised costs agreement and clarify who will actually run the case.

## My recommendation

I would book initial consultations with **Fallu McMillan and Millwater Tyrrell first**, then compare Stanford Legal if the BFA question is central. You can use the same summary of your assets and concerns with each firm to make the advice and fee estimates easier to compare.

One question that would help me narrow this down further: **what makes your property settlement complex?**

For example, is it mainly a family business or trust, several properties or investment assets, a large difference in financial contributions, disputed disclosure, or an existing binding financial agreement? You don't need to share dollar amounts or identifying details.
